recipe: Add the missing variable to the dependency array of your Effect to fix stale-value bugs.
trigger_condition: Your Effect uses a value from the component scope (like a function or variable) but you omitted it from the dependency list, causing the Effect to always use the initial render's value.

recipe: Treat the dependency lint error as a compilation error rather than suppressing it, so you catch stale-value bugs early.
trigger_condition: You are writing a React Effect and the linter flags a missing dependency in the dependency array.
evidence: We recommend treating the dependency lint error as a compilation error. If you don't suppress it, you will never see bugs like this.

recipe: Move event-specific logic (like sending a POST request or showing a notification) out of an Effect and into the corresponding event handler.
trigger_condition: You have logic inside an Effect that should only run in response to a specific user interaction such as form submission.

trigger_condition: A single Effect is fetching or synchronizing multiple independent pieces of data based on different state variables, causing unnecessary re-runs.
evidence: Split the logic into two Effects, each of which reacts to the prop that it needs to synchronize with

recipe: Ensure each Effect represents a single independent synchronization process so that deleting one Effect does not break another's logic.
trigger_condition: You are deciding whether to combine or split multiple pieces of reactive logic into one or more Effects.
evidence: Each Effect should represent an independent synchronization process.

recipe: Extract logic that reads a value you don't want to trigger re-synchronization into an Effect Event, so the Effect only depends on the values that genuinely need to trigger reconnection.

recipe: When a component receives an event handler as a prop that may change identity on every parent render, wrap the call to that handler inside an Effect Event to avoid re-synchronizing your Effect on every parent re-render.
trigger_condition: A parent component passes an inline-defined function as a prop (e.g., an event handler) and you use it inside a useEffect, causing the Effect to re-run on every parent re-render.
evidence: Effect Events aren't reactive, so you don't need to specify them as dependencies. As a result, the chat will no longer re-connect even if the parent component passes a function that's different on every re-render.

recipe: Read values you want to be reactive to inside the Effect, and read values you want to always be the latest (but not trigger re-runs) inside an Effect Event.
trigger_condition: You need an Effect to react to one value (e.g., roomId) but also need the latest value of another (e.g., notificationCount) without re-triggering the Effect when it changes.
evidence: You want your logic to be reactive with regards to `roomId`, so you read `roomId` inside of your Effect. However, you don't want a change to `notificationCount` to log an extra visit, so you read `notificationCount` inside of the Effect Event.

recipe: Whenever possible, avoid passing objects or functions as Effect dependencies; instead move them outside the component, inside the Effect, or extract primitive values out of them.
trigger_condition: You are passing an object or function created in the component body as a dependency of useEffect, causing the Effect to re-synchronize on every re-render because a new reference is created each time.
evidence: This is why, whenever possible, you should try to avoid objects and functions as your Effect's dependencies. Instead, try moving them outside the component, inside the Effect, or extracting primitive values out of them.

recipe: Declare helper functions inside your Effect so they are not treated as reactive dependencies.
trigger_condition: You need helper functions that depend on reactive values and you want to avoid adding them to the dependency array.
evidence: As long as you also declare them *inside* your Effect, they're not reactive values, and so they don't need to be dependencies of your Effect.

recipe: Destructure primitive values from object props outside the Effect and use those primitives as dependencies instead of the object itself.
trigger_condition: A parent component passes an object as a prop that gets recreated on every parent re-render.
evidence: read information from the object *outside* the Effect, and avoid having object and function dependencies

recipe: Call function props outside the Effect to obtain primitive values, then use those primitives as dependencies instead of the function.
trigger_condition: A parent component passes a function as a prop and you want to avoid re-running the Effect on every parent re-render.
evidence: To avoid making it a dependency (and causing it to re-connect on re-renders), call it outside the Effect.

recipe: Use a state updater function (e.g., setCount(c => c + 1)) instead of reading the current state value inside the Effect, so you can remove that state from the dependency array.
trigger_condition: An Effect needs to update a state variable based on its current value, causing an unnecessary dependency.
evidence: If you want to update some state based on the previous state, pass an updater function.

recipe: Split a single Effect into multiple Effects when different parts need to re-run for different reasons.
trigger_condition: Different parts of your Effect depend on different values and should re-run independently.
evidence: If different parts of your Effect should re-run for different reasons, split it into several Effects.

recipe: Move code that responds to a specific user interaction into an event handler instead of an Effect.
trigger_condition: A block of code inside your Effect should only run in response to a specific user action like a click.
evidence: If some code should run in response to a specific interaction, move that code to an event handler.

recipe: Extract an Effect Event from your Effect when you need to read the latest value of a variable without causing the Effect to re-run when it changes.
trigger_condition: You need to access a value inside an Effect but do not want changes to that value to trigger a re-run of the Effect.
evidence: If you want to read the latest value without "reacting" it, extract an Effect Event from your Effect.

recipe: Avoid object and function dependencies in your Effect by moving them either outside the component or inside the Effect body.
trigger_condition: Your Effect's dependency array contains an object or function that is recreated on every render.
evidence: Try to avoid object and function dependencies. Move them outside the component or inside the Effect.
